items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: So he kind of took me under his wing and I got to work in the jazz research library there on campus.

ctx.x: Many times. Many times. Because as you know the West Coast scene of the ‘50s, by the end of the ‘50s there was a definite turning point within the critics and people writing about it where that music was very much dismissed and artists associated with that music got a lot of negative press as well. And so then I would — as doing the research, and you would read things, like you said, you would read these interviews and things about certain artists that just didn’t — when I would meet them and get to know them it…

taskmaster. But you would read about the things people had written and a lot of times it just didn’t match up with the person that I had gotten to know. And over the years I would get to know many of those guys on a pretty close level. Because the type of events, the type of things that I was doing kind of required working closely with them, working closely with them on the music, things like that. And then once you can kind of — the other things that I’m proud of is that I had stayed in — you know I was in music…

because I mean I just couldn’t wait to get in there and catalogue these things and listen to everything and it just — my education was, you know, quadrupled. But I was a Radio/TV/Film major so I got on the student station and became the jazz program director for a couple of years and was able to start to actually be on the radio and kind of learn how to do that, and of course Dick helped me and so on.
